items.description: The Israeli military said it launched strikes on Hezbollah targets in Beirut on Sunday despite ongoing efforts to negotiate an end to the U.S.-Iran war. Smoke could be seen rising over the Lebanese capital. We discuss the latest developments with our correspondent in Tehran, Reza Sayah.

items.title: Will the US-Iran deal be signed on Sunday? What we know so far
items.description: US says a deal to stop the war on Iran could be signed as early as Sunday. Tehran, however, disputes the timeline.

items.title: Britain detains sanctioned oil tanker believed to be linked to Russia's shadow fleet
items.description: Britain is investigating a sanctioned tanker that is suspected of being part of the Russian "shadow fleet," shipping oil in violation of international sanctions over Moscow's war on Ukraine.

items.title: 'The AI war has begun': France and Europe worried as US blocks Anthropic's latest AI model
items.description: The American start-up has disabled its latest AI model, Mythos 5, at the request of Washington. From a European perspective, the decision is seen as evidence of US dominance in the sector and the Trump administration's desire for control.

items.title: Trump to meet with leaders at G7 as confidence grows for Iran war deal
items.description: Pakistan says an agreement to end the Iran war is closer than ever. U.S. President Donald Trump plans to discuss demining the Strait of Hormuz at the upcoming Group of Seven summit that begins Monday.

items.title: Instability, war and closed borders: How aid workers get emergency food to hungry Afghan children
items.description: The odyssey begins in Indonesia and ends, 15,000 kilometres later, in Kabul, the capital of Afghanistan. Along the way, critical food aid destined for young Afghan students crosses nine countries, over land and sea, skirting geopolitical unrest and conflict zones.
